From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@harnett.ai>; Procurement <procurement@harnett.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap & next steps from today - buyflow, packaging, payment routes

Hi Sanjay / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to understand the platform goals and where inference cost predictability matters for Harnett.ai. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align with your purchasing rules: 

Call recap (short):
- Primary use case: real-time summarization and agent assist for enterprise customers (latency-sensitive).
- Likely initial footprint: pilot on hosted API, 10-50k tokens/day; production could move to Dedicated if commit pricing required.
- Data residency: US only for now; private deployment might be needed for EU customers later.

Procurement / payment notes I captured:
- For small pilots (< $5k) you usually use corporate card.
- Anything over the PO threshold (around $25k annually) must go on PO and standard vendor onboarding.
- The team is curious about marketplace (would speed legal & terms).

Action items / next steps:
1) I attached a lightweight pricing summary showing Hosted / Dedicated / Private with example commit tiers and on-demand costs. [Attachment below].
2) Can you confirm the exact PO threshold and whether you require net-30 vs net-45? That will determine how we price a short-term commit vs on-demand for procurement.
3) Please let us know if marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace) is preferred — we can provide SKU-level pricing for that flow.

Attachments: 
- redwood-pricing-summary-20270418.pdf (PDF) – high-level hosted/dedicated/private comparison + sample commit discounts
- SOW-template-redwood.docx (DOCX) – standard SOW we can customize after scope is final

Proposed timeline:
- You confirm PO threshold and marketplace interest by Tue 4/20 -> we send formal pricing tables and a short canary SOW same day.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Marissa and Laura on the pricing table once you confirm procurement details.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwood.com | (415) 555-0112

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps from today - buyflow, packaging, payment routes

Logan — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few points from our side: 

- PO threshold: anything estimated > $25k / year needs to go on a PO and complete our vendor onboarding (W-9, COI, security questionnaire).
- Pilot purchases under $5k we typically run on corporate card to avoid procurement overhead.
- If we can buy via the AWS Marketplace with standard marketplace terms, that shortens legal review substantially — procurement prefers that where available.

For the pricing table please include:
- Line items: Hosted API (on-demand), Hosted API (1-year commit tier), Dedicated (monthly commit options), Private (one-time license + recurring infra ops).
- Show commit discount breakpoints (0%, 10%, 20% at sample commit levels) and expected monthly vs per-token costs.
- Include payment terms options (card, PO net-30, PO net-45).

Timeline from procurement: we can start vendor onboarding the week of 4/26 if we have a ballpark contract value and SOW this week. Emily will be the point for onboarding docs.

Two small asks: 
1) Can you send a marketplace SKU or a Marketplace-ready quote if Redwood is listed?
2) Can you call out any setup/transfer costs for moving pilot->dedicated if we commit within 90 days?

Thanks — cc'ing Emily from finance.

— Sanjay
Co-founder & Head of Product | Harnett.ai
